title: Gate 1: image-loss gradient vs finite differences of supersampled images
description: Kerr, camera at 1000 M, model sky +-22 M, thin disk g^4 F tau, RK4 step fraction 0.01 with the cubic Hermite disk crossing, fp64. Observed 64 x 64 image of 3 uas pixels, theta_g = 3.8 uas/M, PA = 0.4, Gaussian beam 20 and 7 uas FWHM (truncated at 5 sigma). Data: the 2048^2-sample image at (a + 0.04, i + 3 deg, 1.03 theta_g, PA + 0.1); loss 1/2 sum (I - D)^2 / sigma^2 with sigma = 1% of the data peak (a test choice). Method: 512^2 stratified samples with forward-mode (dual) tangents, cells near branch changes or in the top 3% of |dI| (dilated by one) refined 8 x 8. Samples move with the ring flow V = (d rho_c/d theta) g(rho - rho_c) e_rho about the critical curve's centroid (rho_c by 52 bisections on capture along 1440 directions, velocity by central differences at 1e-4, g = (1 - (x/1.5 M)^2)^2): per sample the total derivative dI/dtheta + V . grad I from tangents along (a, i, u, v), plus I grad B . V and B I div V (a change of variables of the image integral; it removes the 1/distance growth of dI/dtheta at the photon-ring subrings, whose square is not integrable). Plus the edge term sum over row crossings of Delta y (I_left - I_right) (dx*/dtheta + (dx*/dy) V_y - V_x), crossings found between neighbours of a 2048 x 1024 regular grid by 48 bisections, dx*/dtheta by bisection at theta +- 1e-5. Truth: central differences of the loss of 2048^2-sample images on two independent jitter sets, averaged (spin and inclination: Richardson extrapolation of h = 3.2e-2 and 1.6e-2, checked against 1.6e-2 and 8e-3; theta_g and PA: 5e-5 relative); the gate also requires the truth's standard error from the two sets to be at most 0.3%. Diagnostics per parameter: the error without the edge term, with the edge term from every other row, of the method's Jacobian contracted with the dense image's residuals (Jacobian error alone), without the ring flow (fixed sky points, the estimator of the first two runs), and with the flow on the unrefined 512^2 base only.
